newsitem.title: USA: Clinton settles on Gambling Commission appointees.
newsitem.headline: Clinton settles on Gambling Commission appointees.

text.p: President Clinton plans to name a Nevada gaming regulator, a former New Jersey state treasurer and an American Indian to a new nine-member gambling commission, a senior White House official said Tuesday.
The official, speaking on condition of anonymity, said Clinton had settled on Bill Bible, Richard Leone and Robert Loescher to be his appointees to the commission created by Congress last year.

Bible chairs the Nevada State Gambling Control Board; Leone is a former New Jersey state treasurer and Loescher is a member of Alaska's Tlingit Indian Tribe. The three will join six others already named to the panel by members of Congress.
Clinton chose the three because he "wants a balanced study of the impact of legalized gambling on the U.S. economy and society at large, the official said.
Bible favors legalized gambling, while Leone and Loescher are known to be personally opposed, the source said.

The gambling industry opposed the passage of legislation that created the commission. It was sponsored by Rep. Frank Wolf, a Virginia Republican, an opponent of gambling, who wanted a study of whether gambling is economically and socially desirable.
The commission will conduct a two-year, $5 million probe of the benefits and liabilities of casino gambling, state-sponsored lotteries, horse racing and sports betting.
